terms.definition: A state in which opposing processes balance, so a system stays within limits although it is constantly changing.
terms.examiner: Stress that the processes continue; it is not a static state.

terms.definition: A change that causes effects which reduce the original change, returning the system towards its original state.
terms.examiner: Example: more carbon dioxide increases photosynthesis, which removes carbon dioxide.

terms.definition: A change that causes effects which increase the original change.
terms.examiner: Example: warming melts ice, lowering albedo, causing more warming.

terms.definition: The point beyond which a system moves to a new equilibrium and does not return when the original pressure is removed.
terms.examiner: Examples: loss of the Amazon rainforest, collapse of ice sheets.

terms.definition: The ability of a system to recover after a disturbance.
terms.examiner: More diverse systems tend to be more resistant to change.
